name: Subcontractor engagement and management
one_line: The paperwork of getting another firm to do part of the works and paying them for it: the enquiry and the comparison of prices, the subcontract order and its scope and programme, the insurances, accreditations and competence evidence demanded before anyone starts, the tax and employment-status paperwork, then the monthly cycle of payment applications, valuations, payment notices and pay-less notices, retention held and released, and the back-charges and terminations when it goes wrong. Its defining property is that the SUBJECT IS ANOTHER FIRM rather than a building: a fitness-to-engage pack assembled about a counterparty's corporate standing, and the apparatus for ending the engagement when it fails. The statutory payment cycle runs through this row but does NOT identify it - construction_property.final-account holds the same application-and-notice pair at head-contract level and the schema claims the underlying cumulative arithmetic for itself, so what separates the two here is which agreement the reference names and which side the holder stands on. Absorbs the legacy row cons.subcontract. Placeholder row (J-IND) at J-DEPTH: it recognises the situation and writes NO field rows, because the construction_property schema declares none.

proposed_fields.example: the site, premises, plot, block or unit an engagement is carried out at - Plot 4 Kilnfield, Unit 3B Harbour Works
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: NOT this row's proposal. A SECOND of the key the construction_property schema row already proposes, recorded here so R1c settles it once rather than per sibling. This row's own datum for that adjudication is a negative one and it cuts against a naive reading of the schema default: this is the sibling where `property` is LEAST often the right root, because the compliance half of the row - a firm's insurances, accreditations and standing - has no property at all. That is not an argument against the key; it is an argument against reading destination_eligible as 'always first'.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Follows the construction_property proposal unchanged; this row does not reopen it. It records only the caveat above, that a firm-level record has no property to branch on and must not acquire one by inheritance from a folder it happens to sit in.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Unchanged from the schema's proposal: an address read from a labelled slot could reach `direct`, but an address is this family's constitutional never-alone and appears here as the site, the subcontractor's registered office, the main contractor's head office and the insurer's address at once. A gazetteer-plus-context rule family would be needed to reach `validated`; R2 owns that rule and this row does not write it.

proposed_fields.example: the works package the engagement delivers - groundworks, M&E first fix, roofing - nested inside a named job
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: NOT this row's proposal. A SECOND of the construction_property proposal, INCLUDING its live alternative that R1c should feel free to take: reuse the canonical `project` instead of minting anything. This row's contribution to that adjudication is the case where the alternative hurts first - a WORKS PACKAGE is an instruction that is not a project and is nested inside one. If `project` is stretched to cover it, one job's five packages either collapse into one value or each become a sibling 'project' of the job that contains them. Stated as the cost, not as an objection; a near-duplicate of a canonical key is the defect D6 exists to kill.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A package name read from a labelled order slot is stronger than one read from a folder name, and folder names are the usual source. Ceiling follows the schema proposal; no rule is written here.

proposed_fields.example: the counterparty firm an engagement record is about - Meridian Groundworks Ltd
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: NOT this row's proposal, and NOT construction_property's either. A SECOND of the key the landed business_operations schema row proposes, and R1c must settle it as ONE decision, there, for every row that wants it. This row's datum is the sharpest available on the whole roster: the entire second leg of this row's node test - the recommended dimensions - wants a COUNTERPARTY-FIRM level, and `client` and `our_firm` between them cannot express it, because the subcontractor is neither. construction_property's own role_split already records that the contractor role has no key; this row records the identical gap from the other end. It mints nothing: minting on a schema that declares no fields, at the exact moment it would be most convenient, is the 574's original mistake performed knowingly. “The system may create new values when it sees a new course, project, company, university, or event, but it should not invent new fields automatically.”
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Follows business_operations' reasoning unchanged and this row does not reopen it. 00's prohibition is directly on point for the temptation this row feels most strongly - “A folder should not become a collection point for everything produced by the same person or organization.” - and a subcontractor-named folder is exactly that collection point.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A firm name read from a labelled party slot on an order is the good case; the ordinary case is a name in a filename or a folder, and this row's never_alone list records that a company name here appears in at least five roles at once. Ceiling follows the business_operations proposal.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal and never an extraction licence. The construction_property schema declares no field rows (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6), so nothing here writes a domain fact; detection exists so the material is recognised, kept where this row’s sensitivity says, and offered honestly. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

the payment-cycle structure, which places a file in THIS FAMILY but does not on its own identify this row - construction_property.final-account carries the same application-and-notice pair at head-contract level and says so in its own recognition, and the construction_property schema claims the underlying 'to date, less previously certified' arithmetic at schema level. It is a supporting signal here, and what it actually contributes is DIRECTION, per that neighbour's own discriminator: 'a subcontract or order reference with the firm as payer supports the subcontract row; the main contract reference with the firm as payee supports this row': a numbered periodic application for payment stating a gross valuation to date, less previously certified, less retention, giving a net sum applied for and a due date — answered by a payment notice or pay-less notice stating a different sum and the basis on which it was calculated, within a stated period. The application-and-answering-notice PAIR is the signal, not either half. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”

a pre-appointment competence and standing pack about ANOTHER FIRM, assembled as a condition of engaging it: employer's and public liability certificates with limits and expiry dates, accreditation or membership certificates, a completed health-and-safety pre-qualification questionnaire, a tax or employment-status verification record, and sometimes a collateral warranty or parent company guarantee. This is the row's strongest carrying structure and the one four separate siblings independently reached for as the discriminator (construction_property.plant-hire: “an engagement to carry out works, with insurances and competence evidence, supports the subcontract row”; construction_property.quote-estimate: “an ORDER framing with an engagement, insurances and competence evidence supports the subcontract row”). Its members are individually unremarkable and collectively diagnostic - “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.” - and nothing else on this schema is about a firm's corporate standing rather than about a building. Provenance: inference.

an engagement-FAILURE sequence, which is distinct from the payment dispute and is claimed by no sibling: a back-charge or contra-charge with a description, a cost build-up and a notice of intention to deduct; then a notice to remedy within a period, a warning of determination, and a final account of works completed by others. construction_property.final-account owns the dispute about a SUM; construction_property.snagging-defects owns defects after practical completion; neither owns the apparatus for ENDING an engagement downward. Provenance: inference.

a subcontract order structure: a numbered order naming a works package, a scope, a lump sum or schedule of rates, a programme or period for the works, retention and payment terms, and the main contract it sits under — back-to-back references being characteristic.
a package comparison or enquiry schedule: a table of subcontractors against a common scope with prices, qualifications, exclusions and a recommendation — the pre-appointment half of the row.

a pre-appointment evidence pack: employer's and public liability insurance certificates with expiry dates, accreditation certificates, a health and safety questionnaire response, competence cards and a tax or employment-status verification reference, held together for one firm.
a retention structure: sums held at a stated percentage, a half-release at practical completion and a balance at the end of a defects period, tracked per package.
a back-charge or contra-charge record: a deduction against a subcontractor's account with a description, a cost build-up and a notice of intention to deduct.
a termination or default sequence: a notice to remedy within a period, a warning of determination, and a final account of the works completed by others.
parent-folder context naming a subcontractor, a works package or a payment application number, treated as a clue once one of the structures above is present. Folder context never fires alone.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: this row holds another firm's prices, its insurance details, its people's competence cards and sometimes the record of its failure. Any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”

the central determination for this row: which SIDE the holder is on. A subcontract order, a payment application and a payment notice are the same documents in every subcontractor's file and every main contractor's file, with the roles reversed and nothing in the document saying whose filesystem it is. This is the same hole business_operations.contract-administration records for buying versus selling.

separating a SUBCONTRACT (labour and works, under the main contract, with a payment-notice regime) from a SUPPLY ORDER (materials delivered, paid on invoice). The paperwork rhymes and the legal machinery does not.

separating an application for payment from an invoice. In construction the application usually comes first and the invoice follows the certified sum, so the same money appears twice in two document families.
an unlabelled engagement: a price emailed by a trade, accepted by reply, with no order and no terms — the commonest real subcontract in small works.

a purpose-coherent package file whose members are individually unremarkable — an order, three insurance certificates, a RAMS pack, six applications and a retention schedule. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
in every case above, abstention is the required outcome where the evidence does not settle it. “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
never_alone: a company name alone. It appears here in at least five roles at once — the subcontractor, the main contractor, the client, the insurer and the accreditation body — and 00 states the same ambiguity for a university: “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” The company case is worse, and this is recorded as inference because 00 writes that sentence about a university, not a company.
a currency figure alone, or a percentage read as retention. Percentages abound: discount, retention, VAT, completion, margin.

a UK-style postcode or a street address alone. An address is the single most tempting token in this whole family and it appears in every role at once — the site, the client’s home, the contractor’s registered office, the architect’s letterhead, a supplier’s depot, and a comparable property cited in a report. 00 states the same ambiguity for a university name: “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” — the address case is worse, and this is recorded as inference because 00 writes that sentence about a university, not an address.
the words “application”, “notice”, “order” or “certificate” alone. Every one of them names a different document family in three other schemas in this roster.
an insurance certificate alone. It is a finance record, a safety pre-qualification document and a subcontract condition simultaneously, and the certificate itself says only that a policy exists.
a numbered reference alone — SC/044, App 07, PO 3311. Prefixes are firm-specific and unstandardised.

source_type or extension alone. “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”, and file_kind_plausible is constitutionally never-alone (CONNECTION section 5, invariant 2).
membership in a download session — a whole project folder or a document-portal export pulled down at once. “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”
a bare 4-digit number read as a year. It is at least as often a drawing number, a job number, a plot number, a house number, a cost code, or a British Standard reference.

a PDF author, producer, or company metadata string alone. “PDF metadata should be treated as supporting evidence, not as truth” — one contractor’s template stamps the same firm on every blank form it ever generated.

one subcontractor across several projects over time — a real reason to group, and the one most likely to tempt a company label onto a bare certificate, which is exactly what must not happen. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”

one order across its revisions, joined by the universal version_family fact rather than by any construction fact.

and the stop rules apply as written — “when members carry irreconcilable course, institution, project, term, or purpose facts”.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: a dimension may only branch on a field the same entry’s schema declares, and construction_property declares none (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6). That is a contract fact, not a claim that this situation has no shape — it plainly does, and it is recorded here as PROSE for whoever answers the schema row’s open_question. The recommendation, held as prose: the project first, then the package or subcontractor, then the function (appointment / compliance evidence / payment cycle / disputes and close-out), with the payment period as an optional fourth level where a package ran long enough to have many. Application 07 is meaningless without knowing whose package on which job — the number repeats everywhere — which is 00's own reason for putting a course above a homework number. One qualification is recorded rather than resolved: a subcontractor's insurance and accreditation certificates belong to the FIRM rather than to any one project, so a corpus with repeat subcontractors will want them once rather than copied into every project branch. 00’s own ordering reason applies: “a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child”. Not time-first — “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” And whatever eventually lands stays a recommendation: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: Reciprocal: the landed row already names this one, on the ground that subcontract administration is its shape in a sector with a statutory notice regime. Repeated here in the same terms. The discriminating evidence: a site, a works package, a valuation number or a statutory payment-notice reference supports this row; a general commercial register and a renewal calendar supports the business row. Provenance: inference.

The load-bearing collision on this row. A supply order and a subcontract order look alike and are paid on entirely different machinery. The discriminating evidence: an application-and-answering-notice pair, retention, and a works package support this row; line items, quantities, a delivery address, a delivery note and payment on invoice support the materials row. Provenance: inference.

Subcontract accounts roll up into the main account, and the same valuation numbers appear on both. The discriminating evidence: a named package and a subcontractor's application support this row; the main contract's interim certificates, the employer's valuations and the closing settlement support the final-account row. Provenance: inference.

Changes cascade down as subcontract variations and claims are defended downward on near-identical paper. The discriminating evidence: a subcontract order reference, an application and a payment notice support this row; a main-contract instruction and a claim against the employer support the variation row. Provenance: inference.

Reciprocal with that row: a subcontractor's RAMS, competence cards and insurances arrive as engagement conditions and are simultaneously safety evidence. The discriminating evidence: an order, an application or a notice supports this row; a hazard matrix, a permit or a briefing register supports the safety row. Provenance: inference.

Package enquiries and tender comparisons are procurement's shape done by a construction team. The discriminating evidence: a works package, back-to-back main-contract terms and a site support this row; a general requirement, an evaluation matrix and an award letter with no site support the procurement row. Provenance: inference.

Approved-subcontractor lists, performance scorecards and insurance expiry trackers overlap this row's compliance half completely. The discriminating evidence: a package, an order and a payment cycle support this row; a relationship-level scorecard with no project anchor supports the vendor row. Provenance: inference.

A subcontractor's application, the invoice that follows it and the tax deduction statement are all bookkeeping entries in the same month. The discriminating evidence: a ledger, a period, a nominal code or a tax return support the finance row; an application-and-notice pair and retention support this row. Because finance is a safety schema, where both fire the protective ordering runs first. Provenance: inference.

Reciprocal, and the landed J-DEPTH spine states this side first; its wording is adopted rather than re-authored. It demoted itself to make room: “Similarly `variation-claim` owns the numbered instruction, `site-diary` owns the dated daily record, and `subcontract` owns the works package. The gist row claimed all of them.” The discriminating evidence: the enquiry, the order, the competence evidence and the payment cycle of engaging another firm support this row; the head contract those packages deliver - the award sequence, the contract-particulars block with possession paired to completion, the programme and the handover envelope - supports the project row. Shared fixture named identically on both sides: Sub-contract order 2431-08 groundworks.pdf. Belonging to a project folder is browse, not activation: CONNECTION.md §3, activation ≠ grouping. Provenance: inference.

The load-bearing cross-schema seam, and it is stated FROM ONE SIDE ONLY: that row landed at J-DEPTH before this family and names no construction_property row, so R1c owes the reciprocal (NJ-CP-SUB-3; construction_property.construction-project records the identical debt). Drawn in that row's OWN idiom so it is not contradicted - it separates itself from finance.household-property, finance.hoa-residents-association and finance.subscriptions-utilities by the same formula each time, instrument versus running apparatus: “Party recitals, reciprocal obligations and an execution block creating or amending duties support this situation; member-account, governance, meeting or routine association-administration structure supports finance.hoa-residents-association.” Read across: party recitals, numbered clauses and an execution block - the signed subcontract instrument, its deed of variation, its collateral warranty, its parent company guarantee - support the legal row, and legal is a safety domain whose protective ordering runs FIRST; the running apparatus around that instrument - enquiry, comparison, competence pack, applications, assessments, notices, retention ledger, contra-charges - supports this row. A signature block, a firm name, an address or a money figure counts for neither, which is that row's own repeated phrasing. Per-evidence-item mutex, not a file-level winner. Shared fixture: SC-044 Meridian Groundworks - order.pdf, which this row already marks also_schema: legal and routes to Protected Records. Provenance: inference.

Reciprocal; that row states this side and its wording is adopted. Operated hire and labour-and-plant subcontracting differ by one clause. The discriminating evidence: an engagement to carry out works, with insurances and competence evidence, supports this row; the supply of a machine at a rate supports the plant row. Provenance: inference.

Reciprocal; that row states this side and its wording is adopted. Subcontractor prices collected to build a quote become subcontract orders if the job lands. The discriminating evidence: an ORDER framing with an engagement, insurances and competence evidence supports this row; an unaccepted price supports the quote row. The shared fixture is this row's own sparse case, RE_ price for the groundworks - ok to proceed.eml, and neither row may manufacture an engagement from an acceptance line. Provenance: inference.

An insurance certificate is the same document whoever holds it, and this row holds other firms' certificates by the dozen. The discriminating evidence: the holder's OWN policies, schedules, renewals and claims support the finance row; a certificate held ABOUT ANOTHER FIRM as a condition of one engagement at one site supports this row. A policy number, an insurer's letterhead or an expiry date discriminates neither. Shared fixture: EL and PL certificates - Meridian.pdf, whose must_not_conclude already forbids reading it as the holder's own. Provenance: inference.

Named on the REFUSED construction_property.timesheet row, which routed its pay reading to that row and its contractual reading here, and this row honours that routing unchanged. The discriminating evidence: a firm-to-firm engagement with an order, an application or a notice supports this row; hours, rates and deductions for the purpose of paying a PERSON support the hr row, under a stricter posture. The genuinely undecided fixture is an agency timesheet - a supply-of-labour billing document that reads either way - and abstention is the correct outcome there rather than a guess. A subcontractor is a firm, not an employee, and treating the two alike is the error employment-status paperwork exists to prevent. Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: Orders, tax deduction statements and comparison schedules carry another firm's commercial position and sometimes a sole trader's personal tax details — a private individual's financial information held by someone else. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The home for a standalone application, notice, certificate or warranty arriving with no package file around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The honest outcome for a retention schedule, a comparison sheet or an acceptance email whose project and side are unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

Remittances, supply orders and isolated invoices are transactional documents rather than engagement records. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

Password-protected pre-qualification packs and portal exports are ordinary here. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

Standard subcontract forms, published notice templates and blank questionnaires are reference material, not records. “Reference Clips may live under Personal/Reference Clips and hold saved visual inspiration, product references, quotes, recipes, short article captures, code snippets, or other material that is useful for later retrieval but does not belong to a current project.”

role_split.why: 00's own role-split pair, and this row is where it fails most visibly, because the engagement has THREE parties and the pair has two keys. The subcontractor is neither the client nor the holder's own firm, yet it is the subject of most of this row's material. This row does not mint a key to close the gap - construction_property's own role_split records it, and the fix is the `organization` proposal seconded above, adjudicated once by R1c. Recorded here so the gap is visible from the sibling that suffers it, not only from the schema.

sensitivity_why: Almost everything in this row is somebody else's commercial information held by the holder: another firm's price, its margin, its insurance limits, its accreditation status, its failures and its back-charges — and, where the subcontractor is a sole trader, that firm is a private individual whose tax deduction statements and competence cards are here too. 00's corpus sentence names those categories: the corpus “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records”. As inference rather than a design claim, the exposed party is normally NOT the user and cannot consent to what the product does with the file, which argues for the cautious setting. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; the handling class is P7's and is not set here.
open_question: Two. (1) Which side of the subcontract the holder is on has no canonical key, and this row is where the hole bites hardest, because the entire payment machinery is directional: an application is something you send or something you answer. business_operations.contract-administration records the same hole as buying-versus-selling and construction_property.survey-valuation as transaction-side; one canonical proposal at R1c should serve all three, and this row mints nothing. (2) Whether a subcontractor's insurance and accreditation certificates belong to the project branch or to a firm-level branch that several projects reference. They expire on the firm's calendar, not the project's, and copying them into every project branch is how a corpus ends up with eleven copies of one certificate and no idea which is current. (3) NEW: legal.leases-agreements landed at J-DEPTH before this family and names no construction_property row, so the instrument-versus-running-apparatus seam is stated from one side only, in that row's own vocabulary and deliberately not contradicting it. R1c owes the reciprocal, using the fixture SC-044 Meridian Groundworks - order.pdf named on this side; construction_property.construction-project records the identical debt, so it is one reciprocal covering both. Leaving it one-sided means the two schemas disagree silently about who takes a signed subcontract, which is the failure reciprocal edges exist to prevent. (4) NEW: whether a purpose-coherent pack can be a DETECTION signal or only a GROUPING mechanism. This row's strongest leg-1 structure is the pre-appointment competence pack, whose members are individually unremarkable and collectively diagnostic; 00 licenses that reading - “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.” - but writes the sentence about an application submission, not about this. If R1c reads purpose-coherence as grouping only, leg 1 loses its stronger half and rests on the engagement-failure sequence alone. The row would probably still stand, and it would stand much more narrowly.
